summary: Latest decision wins: Collective has not approved an Entrata rollout and plans to remain on its current platform, potentially revisiting the decision in 24–36 months. Do not activate a property or change production settings now. The settings below are the consolidated provisional first-property configuration for future use. Later calls also supersede the earlier inspection recommendation: Collective subsequently said it does not use inspections, so inspection templates should remain unconfigured and unit-type generation should be disabled.

Another area here that we want to eliminate and Ar creates a bottleneck for a lot of our customers. Ar can be really complicated. If you have a resident skip mid month, you may have regulations about how to prorate that skip, how to charge accelerated rent or lease termination fees, etc, and whether that's the property manager responsible to make those ledger changes, or if it's a central person that's responsible to make those ledger changes that tends to be a bottleneck as companies grow and as companies scale and it's just not sustainable. You end up having a whole team of Ar accounting supervisors to help clean up the resident ledgers. And our goal as a platform in regard to resident ledgers is 100 percent ledger automation. And I'm going to show you a couple of examples of that I think should be unique compared to every other system in multifamily. So, the first is to just mention that conditional charges are automated, NSF, fees, transfer fees, month to month fees, early lease, termination fees, insufficient notice, fees, lease violation fees, etc. Did I scare the whole room away? Except Marissa? No, the camera focused right on Marissa. She's responsible for this. This is her section. She really likes this one… that is weird on the camera. It's like so… well, NSF is a good example. Let's say Vince pays his rent on the fourth with a checking account and we are checking to make sure the accounts are valid and they've got money, but E, checks can still bounce, right? So he pays on the fourth, we assess late fees. On the fifth, he doesn't get one. He paid on the fourth. And then we find out from the bank on the seventh that his payment was returned to NSF. Now we're your payment processor. So we're going to update the system. We're going to log that payment was NSF and reverse it. But all of the system automation then goes into effect. So it charges the NSF fee automatically. It looks and sees if late fees should have been posted since the date of his payment. So his payment was on the fourth. And so it just runs a little script that says, hey, have we charged late fees since then? And yes, of course, we have on the fifth. And so it backdates and posts the late fee charges that should have been posted to Vince's ledger that occurred in the interim. And then that automatically all takes place. But the opposite is also true. Let's say Vince paid by slipping his check under the door of the leasing office and we didn't notice it or it got set on a desk and forgotten about until the sixth and he paid us on the fourth. And so now you go in, you backdate his payment to the fourth, it reverses the late fee automatically and he doesn't get one. Nobody has to reverse it. Ledgers are automated, 100 percent automated in entrata. And there are just hundreds of examples of how that could work. So, month to month fees start automatically. Renewal charges start automatically. You don't. Have to run an expiring leases report and then try to figure out what everybody's prorated month to month fee should be in the month that their lease expired. And this creates a huge amount of value. First, it reduces administrative burden for Ar. Second, it reduces risk because your ledger matches your lease, we generated the lease. We can ensure that the ledger matches the lease exactly. And that's an exceptionally valuable place or position for your company to be in if you go into a dispute or a court proceeding with a resident. And then finally, it prevents things from getting overlooked or forgotten. If we forget an insufficient notice fee or we enter it at a lower than scheduled amount that's real revenue that was lost. And so almost all clients after moving to entrata, see a significant reduction in the administrative burden, time savings. They see a small marginal improvement in revenue but measurable. And then as far as reductions in risk, they're seeing more accuracy on ledgers. Let me give you another example that I think is just really cool. Let's say Jax had some sort of emergency family situation and he had to move out today. So he comes into the office. It's not a skip. He's coming in. He's letting you know the whole situation. And we've got to move out reason whatever it is family issue and the system then he's already paid for July. It's the sixteenth of July though. And this property is set up to prorate based on move out date by regulation. And so the system is automatically reversing first of month billing that billed from the first to the 30 first. And it's replacing it with a prorated billing of the first through the sixteenth. It's also adding an insufficient notice fee to his lease and scheduling the unit term. And so there's no manual work here. I just place him on notice and click approve. And his ledger now is up to date. And you can see his balance went from zero to 481 dollars because his first of the month payment wasn't enough to cover the newly prorated charges and that insufficient notice fee, it was inadequate and he owes us some extra money. Your staff don't have to do any of those calculations or actions. And in every other system that I'm aware of all of those re, prorations calculations and charges the reversal of the first of month and replacing it with prorations is 100 percent manual. And that makes a big difference as a property of scaling… or property management company like yourselves. Questions about Ar and resident ledgers. There's even more here we just don't have time like all of your post move out notices and write offs automated. If you get a payment after charges are written off, the recovery entries for collecting funds for written off balance. Automated. Entrata is pretty significantly ahead of the industry for Ar automation. A couple other areas that I'll just try to describe that I think are unique advantages without going into too much detail. So entrata is a bit unique because you're not putting in the renewal price for each property manually. Every unit can have a renewal price set up in advance. So if I'm looking at a particular unit type, I've got prospect rents. I've got month to month rents and I've got renewal rents. So maybe you just want to go three percent higher than their current rent across the board or 100 dollars higher than the current rent across the board. You can do that and publish that for the entire property, say on a quarterly basis or what have you, and make individual tweaks for a particular resident if necessary. And so this is where that's like I just renewed my lease in seven seconds. John, like that's what this does. And it doesn't create a whole bunch of extra work for your property staff. They're basically coming into the system and looking for leases to countersign and the dashboard is showing them those leases. So if I come back to my approvals tab on my desktop or my phone, I can see that we have leases to countersign. Both of these are new leases. But otherwise it would say renewal or lease modification here. So renewals is another area of efficiency and improvement in resident experience. Another big one that usually makes a financial difference for our clients is delinquency automation. In most systems. If you have residents that need notices, you're kind of running that report, you're doing a mail merge to try to build out those letters, somebody is kind of locking themselves in their office and printing. These out and mailing those. This allows you to generate every notice for every property in a single workflow and print them in a single print run. Altogether. The system keeps track of which notice each resident has received and which notice is next, and when specifically it is due to be sent. And that's all based on your setup. So this is what I meant when I was chatting toward James a little bit about how entrata truly is complicated. We just have more that you can set up than you might in another system. Okay. They were just worried and if you could send a screenshot of how it looked on a mobile phone, they were just worried with the tabs, what it would feel like and look like.

Just that they didn't like the look of it that's the one overall theme I got from and not as easy to use, which I… get… we knew it was more intuitive than appfolio. That doesn't surprise me from them.

Appfolio is I feel very easy to use there's. Just, I don't know, I think I could figure out entrata too. So I don't have necessarily those same feelings. turns.text: Perfect. So everybody can see my screen there. Yes. All good. Perfect. So I know we have our questions here. And most all of your questions that I've read through are gonna be answered by the workflow of how we do accounting. If you have any questions, stop me, let's deep dive. Let's really find out what questions or why those questions are. But first off, looking at the dashboard, we went over it last time but with the accounting and approvals. So all of your approvals which we set up especially with your users and permissions making sure like you're saying being able to see who has done what, and then being able to approve with different approval routings that I'll show in a second that you can set up and being able to see as invoices come in as journal entries are entered as POS. If you use POS even down to ap payments or even down to charging credits that you can place on the residence ledger, you can set up different parameters and approval routings that can go to one person, two people, just making sure certain situations have multiple eyes on them and then approvals set on them. So all of those will go to that person's dashboard for them to be able to approve or reject based off of different invoices and accounts and what properties they're looking at here and being able to go in like I said and approve and post those invoices, or go ahead and reject that and send it back to the person who it originated from. But starting off with the chart of accounts, we can do cash or accrual basis for your properties. But setting up the chart of accounts here in the master GL tree, you'll have all of your GLS that will import for if you want to make changes to the current GL tree that you have, like I said, that'll have every single GL account in it. With that being a master GL, you can roll up into what we call reporting masks which can have multiple GLS roll up into a GL to show a certain way. But it still feeds into that account that you have for the reporting mask. Any of these are not hard coded based off of the name or numbering. You can change anything that you would like to within your current chart of accounts, your balance tree, income statement, whichever. If you would like to do that, it really is going to be flexible as well as being able to see the history here. So if someone has the permission to go in and change a chart of accounts and they can edit it to it, you are able to see those different edits. Being made by what person when it's being made, what's the field, previous value and new value here. So most all of our system is going to have a history to it, an entire path of who did it, what time, what date and what change they made, especially within the accounting system.
How many master chart of accounts can you have?

So it's just one chart of master chart tree that's why we say put your entire chart of accounts in there, whether it's multiple ones. And then you have your reporting masks that are for lenders or certain ownerships. You can have as many of these reporting masks as you would like.

So right now, due to that, we have a different layout for our corporate chart of accounts. We don't necessarily need different numbers, but they utilize kind of different accounts than our properties. Does entrata, able to house our corporate entity as well as the properties?

Yep. So you would just create that corporate entity as like a reporting mask. And so you just have that one. And then it would read, it doesn't even have to really. So any of these, you could look into them and they're going to have, it just looks like another chart of accounts and it's just different namings, different numberings that you would like and their associates. As you're going through it'll. Still pull in either one. And then you can still report on the reporting mask or the master GL tree together or separate.
Okay.

All right. Chart of accounts. I mean, chart of accounts. I've said it too many times charge codes for your properties can be like I said, whatever the naming is, they are not hard coded. You can also have the priority for how when residents go in and pay their rent, how does that actually hit on the ledger? Does it go to utilities and late fees? Where do you want it to go first? And you can associate those prioritized charge of accounts first and then having it hit rent last. It really is just whatever you want it to be or you have it today. And then with you can go in add additional charge codes. It really just depends on how you're wanting it. This here. I do want to bring up because I know with your… you mentioned Hud and I think Maddie said that you don't specifically use vouchers. I did want to bring it up if you ever did use vouchers or want to have a separate ledger for vouchers as residents come in and bring them in, you can separate the different ledgers out to be able to see and actually enter in those vouchers. That's going to be the same way with straight line for commercial. So we have different lever ledgers that you can create here.

Marissa, maybe I do have to clarify. So we do accept subsidy payments and we do break that out. So they'll see a rent charge of say 300 dollars and a subsidy charge of 200 dollars. So if that rent sub isn't satisfied, they're not going to get late fees when they pay their rent type of thing. But we don't have subsidized like low income housing projects, right?

Yep. Perfect. So for those units that you have set up for those ones that you accept, they would just pay to payment to the subsidy ledger. Then obviously the resident will have their ledger that they owe however much that amount is for the rent minus the subsidy.
Okay.

Yeah, of course. Well, as everybody's getting ready, start off by, like can everyone see my screen here? We can deal with that. Okay… perfect. So obviously we've gone over a couple of demos with Marissa and James and some of the onsite teams, but really coming in on especially seeing the dashboard being able to understand how we configure the dashboard is all based off of like we've said before user information. So I am an admin user. So I have every single product housed within my dashboard to be able to complete tasks, to be able to search for any of the accounting, to be able to see all of the residents. And down here, you'll be able to see all of these tabs are going to be task based. So anytime there is an actual to do or a list of something that has happened within the system, they will come into this actual dashboard to be completed. You'll see all these numbers here with different colorations. Obviously with the approvals, that's going to be more important for you guys in understanding accounting for POS invoices, how the budget is done for the budget, worksheets, charges, and credits. So we can pare down or guardrail as much as we need to within the system based off of the user as well as the group. So if you're allowing for the on site teams to add charges or credits to an actual resident ledger, do you want to set guardrails for that? Or do you want them to not be able to add a certain GL code or add a certain charge without an approval process? And we can set those up to make those as robust as you would like. Or we can make them as simple or nonexistent as you would like. For example, in the system, you'll see we have cards and credits on top of resident ledgers are set up for, you have to approve it over a zero dollar amount. So anytime I add one dollar as a charge, one dollar as a credit onto the system or onto a resident's ledger, I actually have to have someone who has the permission to approve it to be able to have that on the actual resident's ledger. And then if I remove something, it's also going to require that approval process. But we're also going to be able to have trails and histories within the entire system. So that anytime you have a question about where this charge go or who actually reversed this off or who've added this, we'll always have timestamps as well as based off of the user who added those in. So even with these approvals, here, you'll be able to see invoices journal entries. But if I look into these invoices right here, all the invoices that have been inputted need an approval process. I can go in and be able to see it's for this property or this GL account. There's a description and there's an amount. I can always go through and approve all of these invoices or I can reject all of them or I can look into them individually. But as well as anything within our system that is blue is drillable. So it's a hyperlink into the information that you're thinking. So if I want to drill into this individual invoice, I would be able to go in and see for the property, be able to see the accounts in the description here. And also additional information down at the bottom. If it's been approved. I can also see this is within the entire invoicing process. If you have your budgets within the system, I can then go in and be able to see month to date as well as year to date here for invoices, journal entries, and what's the actual variance due to the dollar amount and percentage amount. And then being able to actually drill into this 11,000 per year to date. So where did I get that total within all of these invoices that have been posted directly to here? Perfect. And then also calling out. Obviously, I didn't say this in the beginning and that's one of our biggest things, but it's kind of a level set with what you have today. It is a single sign on database. So everything you're needing to do within the system is truly within your dashboard. And like I said, your dashboard will be pared down to exactly what you're needing on a day to day basis that is set up based off of the users and groups and your users and permissions. So you can have an unlimited number of users and groups and being able to see what those actual permissions are and what actual assignments of properties they have access to. So say you want a leasing agent to have three properties that they can lease on. You can give them that ability here. But you can also go into the actual permissions and being able to see the entire dashboard here. And anything that's grayed out is what they don't have, but say an assistant manager is now going to cross train to be a manager and you're allowing them to pay invoices, you can go into the actual accounting portion and be able to allow access and just give them access to invoices. And they can't approve them or anything like that. You can just give them access to actually enter them and create them… questions so far. Nope. We're good, cool. Perfect. So like I said, here within the dashboard, it'll be pared down but also within over here the quick links. So being able to quickly create an invoice upload, invoices, closing a period, advancing the period. All of that can be set up over to the right with quick links calendars. These are really for the onsite teams, but being able to go right here and say, hey, I want to look at all of my properties or just two of my properties. These tabs up here are going to adjust based off of what filter set I've used for those properties or a property list. So say you have a problem group of properties. You can set those up in the system for three four five of those properties and be able to create that property list. And then being able to see leads that haven't been reached out to or neglected or residents that haven't been reached out to because they have hot type news over here to be able to see lease started or renewals that they're reaching out about. So all of this can be done to the dashboard. And each of these colorations here are going to be based off of time periods. So say, an onsite team member enters in an invoice, it's been sitting there, hasn't been approved after a couple of hours. You've set, it goes into yellow which is going to be important. And if it still hasn't been approved after say 1,224 hours, it would go into this red color here which is going to be urgent. It's just making sure that when you're logging in every day, the red is going to be those portions that you need to complete first. And then the yellow which is important and then getting to those gray. So those invoices that are red are going to be sitting there the longest. Perfect. So now getting into kind of how we were talking about the charges and how we do move outs for the actual resident lifecycle. So moving them in moving them out. How do actual charges and credits work? Once an actual lease has been completed and signed by an actual future resident, we want to make sure that all charges recurring one time are all that are in your actual lease, are implemented into your charges and credits within the system so that you're not having to go in manually and enter those whether that's your late charges, that is, your rent, amenities, your NSF, fees, all of those are going to be in your actual recurring charge and credits as well as concessions. So if you're adding a concession and you want it to hit for the second month and you want it to hit for the last month. And you want to stagger those, you can set up those based off of time periods within the lease and the system will automate all of those. But as well as what we call one time charges and credits for conditionals. So like I said, for NSF fees, if a resident has paid on time, their funds bounce after the late date, we can process an NSF fee to the actual ledger as well as a late fee as well as the actual rent. And we can lock them out of their actual portal to where they can't pay on time. So those are all system settings. You can have as many of these conditional fees as you would like. Like you see here as well with like month to month fees or transfer fees, so that you're not having to go back and add those fees or audit those fees because they're already doing this charge timing in the front end as well as with those recurring charges and credits. So making sure if you have pest control trash, the normal things that your on site teams have for each of your residents, those are automated within basic times. How do you guys manage this today? As far as like charge timing, when charges hit the ledger? What type of charges hit the ledger?

Appfolio has a similar setup with monthly charges where we can kind of set up either credits or charges to charge kind of when we want based off dates. And then we can add like manually, any credits or charges that we need in one time.
Okay. Is that the same for like late fees or amenity charges as well? And that they can automatically post?
Correct. We can build that into the property settings so we can have late fees and nsfs charge automatically. Yeah.

I do have a question for you guys. I just would love to hear your thoughts. Like what do each of you, I guess, how involved are you in the move out process as far as like reporting and accounting goes?

I'd say we're pretty involved. It's ultimately the sites who will be the ones to post the charges, but we review it for accuracy and then actually process the move out. So send the disposition letter or refund if necessary.
Okay. Somewhere in the back end.
Yeah.

Okay. So, well, let's work the scenario of a move out and adding a charge or credit onto the actual system. If I'm going into a resident's actual profile here, I am able to add a charge or credit or a payment here. If you're doing a manual payment within the system, but I can go in, add a charge for say we went in and we're doing repairs for a dishwasher and the resident has done that actual damage to it. I can go in and put notes in here for the dishwasher being damaged. But as soon as I add this charge, like I said, we have approvals on for zero dollars, which is giving me anxiety here. I can go through and approve this directly from here because I have the permission, but with our system, it's all in real time so that damage charge is automatically going to populate to this actual resident. So if I go in here and see who put this on, obviously, it's me, I have the time stamp and everything I have where the GL details are allocations and approval history. I can also go in and be able to edit this charge. So if I want to lessen this charge or if I'm going to completely reverse this charge out, I can do all of that directly through the.
Approval process.

And I'll go ahead and approve this and set it through approval routing again. So I'll go ahead and prove that. But as soon as I make those changes that has dropped off of this actual ledger, but I still can see where I added that damage on and I reversed it off and who actually reversed it off. So we're always, like I said, going to have that history and going to have that workflow of understanding who actually did it when they did it so that you're understanding if somebody is taking off charges or if we need to guard rail something that is currently happening, we can definitely do that. Perfect. Any.

callsUsed.title: Discovery Call with Collective
callsUsed.brief: The company is evaluating Entrata as a potential replacement for Appfolio, primarily due to pain points in reporting, accounting, and marketing integrations, especially as they anticipate significant growth. The team discussed current workarounds, desired improvements in reporting and budgeting, and the need for a system that can handle both cash and accrual accounting, as well as potential third-party management. An Entrata demo is scheduled for next week to address these concerns and showcase the platform's capabilities.

callsUsed.title: Onsite DEMO and Lunch with Collective + Entrata
callsUsed.brief: "Entrata presented their platform to Collective, highlighting features for lead management, renewals, maintenance, accounting, and reporting, with a focus on automation and integration to improve efficiency and reduce manual processes. Collective expressed interest in Entrata's AI capabilities, customizable website options, and integrated insurance solutions, particularly for streamlining renewals, managing permissions, and improving financial reporting. The call concluded with a discussion of insurance options and a planned break before continuing the demo."

callsUsed.title: Demo on Accounting + Commercial with Collective
callsUsed.brief: The call was a comprehensive demonstration of Entrata's accounting and reporting capabilities, with Marissa and her team evaluating its suitability for their needs. Key topics included audit logs, implementation timelines, chart of accounts, approval routings, vendor management, fixed asset tracking, invoice management, bank reconciliations, budgeting, month-end closing, management fee calculations, and reporting features. Marissa's team will debrief and send follow-up questions to determine the next steps, including potential demos of commercial features and the Business Intelligence tool.

callsUsed.title: Pricing call with Entrata+ Collective
callsUsed.brief: The call was a pricing proposal presentation by Entrata to Collective, covering various software solutions and services. Collective will reconvene to decide which areas, such as rewards programs, rent reporting, and business intelligence, they want to explore further, with Entrata following up next week. Entrata is the only vendor Collective is currently considering.

callsUsed.title: Collective Lunch Demo w/ Entrata
callsUsed.brief: The call was a software demo of Entrata, covering commercial property management, maintenance, leasing, and bill pay features, with Marissa and James from the client side expressing interest in specific functionalities and addressing current pain points with their existing system, Appfolio. The Entrata team showcased various features, including tenant portals, work order management, and automated bill payment options, while also addressing pricing and implementation questions. The call concluded with a break scheduled to resume with a discussion on Business Intelligence.

callsUsed.title: Collective and Entrata, Project/Demo Recap + Next Steps
callsUsed.brief: The Entrata team is working to secure a partnership with Marissa's company, despite their current contract with atfolio. Marissa's team is impressed with Entrata, but the leadership team needs to be convinced, and James needs to be won over regarding the maintenance side of the platform; Entrata is offering to explore contract buyout options and provide resources to address concerns and facilitate the decision-making process, with a follow-up meeting scheduled for December 30th.

callsUsed.title: Collective+ Entrata Sync
callsUsed.brief: The call focused on planning an upcoming on-site Entrata software demonstration for Marissa's team, addressing their concerns about the transition process, pricing, and training, and discussing how Entrata can meet their needs, including revenue management and business intelligence. They agreed to involve Entrata specialists and provide references to alleviate concerns, with a focus on demonstrating the ease of transition and long-term benefits of switching from Outfolio. Marissa will work on a pricing comparison, and Entrata offered assistance to ensure accurate information and address any questions before she presents it to her team.

callsUsed.title: Collective Pricing Sync
callsUsed.brief: The call focused on Entrata's proposal to replace Marissa's company's current systems, addressing concerns about the transition and highlighting the benefits of Entrata's all-in-one platform, including new features and potential cost savings. They discussed timelines for implementation, pricing, and marketing services, and scheduled demos for key team members, including accounting, maintenance, community managers, and a new asset manager, with a follow-up meeting planned to sync on pricing and potentially involve Entrata's executive team.
